finite_default_domain.definition: All 49 seed positions in the native 7x7 framed interior.
finite_default_domain.scope: Default native parameter distribution only; finite input count is not inflated by repeated sampling.

provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The generator draws a hollow square frame in colour 3 on a background of colour 0. Inside the frame is a 7x7 interior holding a single seed pixel, also colour 3. Every interior cell is coloured by the parity of its Chebyshev distance to the seed: odd distances become 4, even distances become 2. The emitted program works directly in the visible grid.

1. It finds the largest 4-connected component of colour palette[3]. A seed touching the frame merges into it, which does not change the frame's bounding box.
2. It shrinks that bounding box by one cell on each side to get the interior.
3. Every non-background cell inside the interior counts as a seed.
4. Each background interior cell gets its minimum Chebyshev distance to a seed. Odd distances become palette[4] and even distances become palette[2].

Chebyshev distance, square frames and bounding boxes are all unchanged by rotation and reflection. So the mechanism is the same in every D4 orientation, and d4 needs no axis or direction specialisation. Only the colour roles are specialised, as palette[0], palette[3], palette[4] and palette[2]. The 15x15 grid stays square under D4, and the rectangular-grid logic is generic anyway.
draft_notes.limitations: d4 is deliberately unused because the rule is fully isotropic. The program assumes the frame is the largest single-colour component of palette[3], which always holds in the generator's domain. If there were several seeds, the nearest one would be used, as in the archived solver; the generator always produces exactly one. I found no fixture contradictions and no constructor indexing defects or hidden tie-breaks. I have not run any tests.

independent_source_review.mechanism: The input is a fixed 9x9 hollow frame of colour palette[3] (rows 2-10, cols 3-11 in native coordinates) on a 15x15 grid with background palette[0]. One seed pixel of the frame colour sits in the 7x7 interior. Each interior background cell takes palette[4] if its Chebyshev distance to the seed is odd and palette[2] if it is even. The seed cell itself stays the frame colour.
evidence: Constructor: the seed is at (prow+3, pcol+4) with prow, pcol each in 0..6, so it is always strictly inside the interior. The interior loop sets output[3+r][4+c] = 2 if max(|prow-r|, |pcol-c|) % 2 == 0, else 4. The seed cell is then overwritten with 3 in both grids. Nothing about the label depends on hidden randomness beyond the visible seed position.

The validate() parameters reproduce the approved fixtures. Pair 1 (5,1) gives seed (8,5); pair 2 (3,3) gives (6,7); pair 3 (0,5) gives (3,9); the test (2,0) gives (5,4). I spot-checked rows of pairs 1 and 3 and the test against the parity formula; they match.

Factory solver, frame detection: it takes the largest 4-connected component of FRAME. The frame has 32 cells; the seed is either merged into it or is a 1-cell component, so the frame always wins. Because the seed lies inside the frame, it never changes the bounding box. Shrinking the box by one cell gives exactly the 7x7 interior.

Factory solver, seed detection: seeds are the non-BG cells inside the interior. The constructor places nothing else there, so this is exactly the seed. Every BG interior cell is coloured ODD/EVEN by Chebyshev parity, and the seed cell is left unchanged. This reproduces the constructor's output exactly.

Augmented coordinates: the solver works directly on the visible grid. Bounding-box detection, interior shrink and Chebyshev distance are all D4-invariant. A rotated or reflected frame, such as rows 3-11 or rows 4-12, is located generically. There is no untransform/retransform wrapper; d4 is unused because no orientation constant is needed.

Colours: the specialised roles (palette[0], [3], [4], [2]) are genuine rule colours, and both ring colours appear in every demonstration. The odd→4 / even→2 parity is visibly taught; for example, pair 2's distance-1 ring is 4. This is not an arbitrary lookup, and the task is not in the colour-evidence check list.
Host audit: passed, with 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks and 16 fixture variants. There were 49 unique base inputs, which equals all 7x7 seed positions.
nonblocking_limits: The solver uses the nearest of several seeds if more than one were present. This is out of domain, since the constructor always places exactly one.
The solver uses a hard-coded BG constant rather than inferring the background. This is consistent with the palette-specialised domain.
The frame is assumed to be the largest FRAME-coloured component. This always holds in the constructor's domain.
The input space is small: 49 base inputs, all enumerated by the host audit. This is a property of the original task, not a defect.

draft_notes.host_review: Read the independent mechanism, evidence, limitations and context requirements. D4 uses horizontal reflection then clockwise rotation, with the same bijective palette throughout the episode; contradictory D4 contexts are rejected. Native-domain checks and per-episode execution remain mandatory. No hidden output access or normalization wrapper was identified.
